messages.subject: adding frames to facet_grid
parts:
Is there a limit on the frames of plots you can add in facet_grid? I am trying to add four additional sites to the ones I already have plotted. In order to make it work, I had to make my sites factors, and then my data is organized by isotope carbon and year. The code I used is

> Hex_ALL.sites.Littoral$Site <- factor(Hex_ALL.sites.Littoral$Site, levels=c("Matt US", "Matt DS", "LL RES", "GH US", "GH DS", "KAP US", "KAP DS", "Kap FF", "Miss Ref"))
> ggplot(Hex_ALL.sites.Littoral,aes(x=as.factor(Year),y=d13C)) +ylim(-36, -24) +geom_boxplot()+facet_grid(~Site)+ theme_bw() +labs(x="years (by site)") + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90)) + theme(legend.position="none")

I really like that I can lay all my sites out in one row, and would prefer to keep it that way. I have an even larger data set (more years of data) for the same sites, and am wondering if I am asking too much out of R to plot them that way?
Thank you for your help!

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: adding frames to facet_grid
parts: > Is there a limit on the frames of plots you can add in facet_grid?

Don't think so. Might get a bit ugly to look at all in one row though.

I used read.table to read your CSV and then just cut and pasted the
commands you gave:

> > Hex_ALL.sites.Littoral$Site <- factor(Hex_ALL.sites.Littoral$Site,
> levels=c("Matt US", "Matt DS", "LL RES", "GH US", "GH DS", "KAP US",
> "KAP DS", "Kap FF", "Miss Ref"))
> > ggplot(Hex_ALL.sites.Littoral,aes(x=as.factor(Year),y=d13C))
> +ylim(-36, -24) +geom_boxplot()+facet_grid(~Site)+ theme_bw()
> +labs(x="years (by site)") + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90)) +
> theme(legend.position="none")

and I got a graph with nine individual plots in one row, so no problem.

Which would suggest that you have maybe done something before plotting;
subsetting of data or recoding of sites?

Hope this helps get you on track.

Ron.
